text:
infra-monitor: ALARM — nvlink/flap rate spike on us-west-2-gpu-cluster. 6 GPUs reporting intermittent link down events and AER resets, elevated job latencies.

nora: seeing weird slowdowns on <train-job-142>. throughput dropped ~45% around 14:12 UTC.

omar: yup, same. dmesg on node gpu-node-27 shows repeating Xid entries. snippet: `NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.` and `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31`

liam: i pulled the node logs: `nvlink: link 1: remote side down`, `AER: Corrected error received: status=0x00000001` — frequency looks like every 2-5 minutes.

sarah: how many nodes affected and which region? we just committed reserved capacity for us-west-2 this quarter.

infra-monitor: affected hostnames: gpu-node-27, gpu-node-28, gpu-node-41 (all in us-west-2a). 6 physical GPUs total showing flaps.

jessie: quick triage: can someone run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,LINK` and `dmesg | grep -i Xid -n | tail -20` and paste outputs? also `lspci -vvv | grep -i AER -A5` to see PCIe AER details.

omar: pasted minimal output: `GPU 0: Link down count: 23`, ECC correctable errors incremented by 12 in last 6h.

liam: looks like the NVLink lanes are intermittently going down which triggers kernel-level PCI recoveries (hence the Xid). could be flaky riser / slot / root port or a firmware issue.

chip-ops: next steps proposal — cordon + drain gpu-node-27/28/41, move active jobs to alternate pool. run a cold reboot and re-test. if flaps persist, reseat GPUs and risers, then swap to spare hardware.

nora: draining will impact 8 training hosts. can we avoid whole-node drain by isolating affected GPUs? our k8s setup schedules per-device but not multi-sched. draining seems safest short term.

sarah: cost note: draining 3 nodes for maintenance will shift workload to on-demand capacity and increase spend. prefer to batch this in next maintenance window unless risk of job failures goes up. what’s the failure rate?

omar: some jobs are starting to error with CUDA errors after repeated Xid 31. risk of silent corruption is growing. i'd push for immediate cordon of the worst node (gpu-node-27) and an immediate reboot for amd nodes.

jessie: agreed with omar: cordon gpu-node-27 now, move top-2 latency-sensitive jobs. i’ll create a short maintenance tag so autoscaler won't terminate in the middle.

infra-monitor: actioned: cordoned gpu-node-27 at 14:35 UTC. jobs migrated.

chip-ops: after reboot: `dmesg` still shows `AER: Uncorrected error` on pci 65:00 -> opened hw ticket. recommending RMA for GPU in slot 2 if reseat didn't help.

vendor-bot: Vendor ticket created (#VRM-10293). Requested full dmesg, nvlink logs and `nvidia-bug-report.sh`. ETA for engineer review: 24h. please attach power cycling history.

liam: potential software mitigation while we wait: lower NVLINK utilization (reduce NCCL P2P lanes) or force NCCL to fall back to PCIe by setting `NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=GROUP` and `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=^eth0`? not ideal but can reduce cross-gpu nvlink chatter.

nora: can we set scheduling to avoid colocating cross-gpu NVLink-dependent shards on suspected hosts? i can update gang-scheduler rules to prefer other AZs for now.

sarah: do it. prefer scheduling change + single-node cordon over mass downtime. monitor cost impact and report.

chip-ops: hardware note: repeated AER + nvlink flaps often trace back to one of: riser cable contacts, PCIe root complex firmware, or bad GPU silicon. if reseat + firmware patch don't fix, RMA. we have 2 spare risers for us-west-2 rack7 if needed.

jessie: logging checklist for vendor: `dmesg`, `journalctl -k`, `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ECC,LINK`, `lspci -vvv` and `nvidia-bug-report.sh`. also record last 3 reboots and power-cycle timestamps. attaching now.

infra-monitor: telemetry: job latency metric recovered ~10% after cordon and migration, but node-28 still noisy.

omar: will try reseat on node-28 tonight during low-traffic window and run looped stress (`nvidia-smi stress`) and nvlink test.

vendor-bot: vendor asked for firmware versions: `GPU BIOS: 94.02.7A.00`, `Driver: 525.85.12` — provided. vendor commented: "If logs show repeated Xid + AER we recommend trying firmware update + riser swap; escalate to RMA if persists."

liam: note for runbook update: add quick check `dmesg | grep -E "Xid|nvlink|AER"` and a step to cordon single-node if Xid>10 in 1h. also add guidance on when to open RMA (reseat+reboot fail).

jessie: I'll draft the runbook and post in /docs/incidents.

nora: thanks. will monitor nodes and update thread if reseat changes status.

infra-monitor: summary: immediate action — cordon gpu-node-27, migrate hot jobs, schedule reseat on node-28 tonight, open vendor RMA for persistent hardware, update runbook. ongoing: watch ECC counters and nvlink down_count.

sarah: keep weekly cost impact update coming. if RMA causes extended capacity loss, we escalate to sales/finance for credits. :phone: 

chip-ops: adding hardware spares to rack7 and reserving a tech for tomorrow AM.

nora: follow-up: after reseat, node-28 link-down count fell from 19 -> 2 in a 3h stress test. holding for 24h before RMA decision.

omar: nice. closing immediate risk for now. leaving tickets open until 48h stable.

jessie: closing loop — updated runbook PR and linked vendor ticket. thanks all. :thumbsup:
